// c1alloc: stop-the-world under load, with workers that allocate. Four workers loop until main has forced eight
// collections, each iteration allocating a small slice (an allocation is a point where a goroutine can be
// stopped); the runtime must stop all four for each collection while they are running.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"runtime"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
)

var sink atomic.Pointer[[]byte]

func main() {
	const workers = 4
	runtime.GOMAXPROCS(workers)
	var stop atomic.Bool
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for w := 0; w < workers; w++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for !stop.Load() {
				b := make([]byte, 64)
				sink.Store(&b)
			}
		}()
	}
	before := new(runtime.MemStats)
	runtime.ReadMemStats(before)
	const k = 8
	for i := 0; i < k; i++ {
		runtime.GC()
	}
	after := new(runtime.MemStats)
	runtime.ReadMemStats(after)
	stop.Store(true)
	wg.Wait()
	fmt.Printf("gc forced %d, at least %d collections: %v\n", k, k, after.NumGC-before.NumGC >= k)
	fmt.Println("workers", workers, "done")
}
